champion.name: dualtrend
champion.hypothesis: Two trend-following ledgers: USDT side buys strength and sells for USDT profit; BTC side sells weakness and buys back for BTC profit. Gains net of fees and tax; trailing floors; hard stop.

lastEvaluation.diagnosis: The 180d backtest underperforms both benchmarks (USD +4.9% vs static 6.2% vs B&H 12.4%) and BTC equity is actually negative (-6.7%) while price rose +12.4% B&H — the strategy is bleeding BTC, not just USD. Fees (3.01) and tax (7.58) on 1000 capital are small (<1.1% combined) and cannot explain the -6.7% BTC shortfall, so fee drag is NOT the primary cost. The real signature is in openLots: 100% of open lots (5/5 = usdtSide 3 + btcSide 2) are classified trackB, carrying unrealisedUsd of -44.3 (-4.4% of equity) at snapshot — i.e. capital is parked in adverse-entry lots that never reached +1% to start trailing, sitting near a very wide hardStop (0.422 = 42%!) for extended periods. That parked, underwater capital is exactly what turns a positive BTC price move into negative BTC equity. Compounding this, regimeShare shows the system spent 59% of bars in "grid" (choppy/no-trend) and only 21% in "moon" (real uptrend), and the live snapshot shows daily=1, weekly=1 but agree=0 while candidate=moon and active=grid — i.e. the 2-of-3 gate is being denied by the 5m confirmation/dwell logic even when both daily and weekly regimes agree, so the system keeps trading (and pyramiding, atrStepMult=0.7 is fairly tight/aggressive) into chop, seeding new trackB lots that then need the full hardStop distance to resolve. This is a parking + false/slow-regime-confirmation problem feeding each other, not a fee or tilt-sizing problem (tilt score 0.43 vs target 0.59 is a modest, not extreme, mismatch).
hypotheses: Claim: Track B lots are parked too long against a 42% hardStop; tightening hardStop and floor/ratchet thresholds will cut parked unrealised drag and lift BTC-denominated equity without materially reducing trade count.

Claim: Entries during falsely-active "grid" regime (59% of bars) despite daily/weekly agreement drive most trackB lot creation; requiring longer confirmation/dwell and slower pyramid steps will reduce trade count and trackB incidence, trading some upside for lower drawdown and less BTC bleed.
